title: Studying Different Modes of Fluxionality on Pt Nanoparticle Surfaces using In Situ Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Platinum (Pt) nanoparticles (NPs) are widely used as catalysts for energy conversion reactions, and enhancing their catalytic performance requires a fundamental understanding of the reactant-metal interface and, consequently, the metal surfaces under reaction conditions [1, 2]. Additionally, NPs possess unique catalytic properties that differ from their bulk counterparts [3]. Under some conditions, Pt NPs may be structurally less stable and exhibit fluxionality phenomena, undergoing dynamic structural changes such as facet reconstruction, atomic rearrangement, and shape fluctuations [4]. Despite these observations, a detailed understanding of the nanoscale factors leading to different fluxionality modes and their effects on catalytic reactions remain unclear. This work characterizes several modes of fluxionality on the surface of Pt NPs under varying temperatures using in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
